finding.claim: Embed domain allowlist fails open when allowed_domains is empty, so any https host is fetched server-side (SSRF) and its HTML is emitted.
finding.source: Untrusted Markdown: any https:// URL on its own line.
finding.sink: OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:43 getMulti (server-side fetch); EmbedRenderer.php:33 raw embed output.

trace.note: Requires URL to be alone on the line
Only top-level embeds are passed to the adapter
Domain filter installed only when list is non-empty; with default, no host restriction
Fetches the URL from the server

finding.guards_checked: https-only check and standalone-line check (EmbedStartParser), top-level check (EmbedProcessor). None restrict the host. Opt-in: extension requires an explicit adapter.

finding.claim: Embed HTML from the fetched remote page is emitted raw, bypassing html_input and disallowed_raw_html filtering.
finding.source: Remote page content for an allowed host; allowed-domain match is suffix-based, so any subdomain of a shared-hosting domain listed as allowed is attacker-controllable.
finding.guards_checked: html_input filter (HtmlBlockRenderer.php:44-46, HtmlInlineRenderer.php:44-46) not applied to Embed nodes. DisallowedRawHtmlRenderer wraps only configured inner renderers. Unverified: whether upstream embed library places attacker-controlled markup in code.html.

finding.claim: Domain allowlist checks only the initial hostname; HTTP redirects or DNS resolution to internal addresses are not re-checked, enabling SSRF through an allowed domain.
finding.source: Markdown embed URL on an allowed domain that redirects (open redirect) or resolves to an internal IP.

trace.note: Filter applied to the initial URLs only
Fetch follows whatever the library follows

finding.guards_checked: Host equality and suffix match only. No IP-range or redirect-target validation. Unverified: whether the embed library follows redirects by default.

finding.claim: Default configuration renders raw HTML (html_input=allow) and unsafe link/image schemes (allow_unsafe_links=true), so untrusted Markdown can produce javascript: links and script tags unless callers override both settings.
finding.source: Untrusted Markdown input, e.g. [x](javascript:alert(1)) or raw <script> blocks.
finding.sink: LinkRenderer.php:47-50 href output; HtmlBlockRenderer.php:44-46 and HtmlInlineRenderer.php:44-46 raw HTML output.

trace.note: Unsafe-link check runs only when allow_unsafe_links is false

finding.guards_checked: RegexHelper::isLinkPotentiallyUnsafe (RegexHelper.php:251-259) is correct but gated by the config flag. Matches CommonMark spec default; informational.

finding.claim: With an empty attribute allowlist only on* attributes are stripped, so arbitrary non-event attributes such as style, srcdoc, and formaction pass through.
finding.source: Untrusted Markdown attribute syntax, e.g. {style=...} on a generated element.
finding.guards_checked: Attribute name regex (AttributesHelper.php:176) and Xml::escape on values. No script path found beyond what raw HTML already allows; mainly style/UI injection.

finding.claim: Nested quantifiers in ATTRIBUTE_LIST may cause catastrophic backtracking on unclosed attribute lists containing many # characters.
finding.source: Untrusted Markdown line such as {#a#a#a... with no closing brace.

trace.note: (\s*(...)\s*)+ with #[^\s}]+ alternative that can split at each #
matchInPlace runs the regex at each { position

finding.guards_checked: pcre.backtrack_limit bounds each attempt, so this is per-position CPU cost, not unbounded. Unverified: not tested, no shell available.

finding.claim: Mention identifier is inserted into the URL template without encoding, so a permissive identifier pattern lets users alter the destination path, query, or host.
finding.source: User text matched by the administrator-configured mention identifier pattern.
finding.sink: Mention URL via sprintf at StringTemplateLinkGenerator.php:30, rendered as a link.

trace.note: Identifier taken from the regex submatch

finding.guards_checked: Prefix word-boundary check (MentionParser.php:59). Identifier validity is fully config-dependent. Low severity.
